# [mods] Intake, exhaust and tuning

> **[Unverified]** This page rests on a single community report. Cross-check before relying on it.

> Items marked **[Partial]** are only partly confirmed by the source and need more work. They stay in the review queue and are firmed up, corrected or removed as more sources come in.

## Summary

[Partial] Replace broken or stretched stock exhaust studs with new OEM short studs and nuts. [t1089]

Install FelPro gaskets between headers and cylinder head, place a flat gasket at the collector-to-cat junction, then use a round crush gasket on the cat's Y-pipe connection. [t1089]

## Procedure

> **[Partial]** Needs more work: the verifier could confirm only part of this procedure (the steps marked [Partial], or whether the list is complete). Steps or precautions may be wrong or missing; read the source thread before relying on it. Later runs fill it in as more sources are found.

1. Remove the old exhaust studs from the block using an E10 (external Torx) socket.
2. [Partial] Replace broken or stretched stock studs with new OEM short studs and nuts.

_Procedure reported by [t1089]._

<details><summary>Alternate procedure [t1089] [Partial]</summary>

1. Install FelPro gaskets between the headers and cylinder head.
2. Place a flat gasket at the collector-to-cat junction.

</details>

## Tools

- E10 / External Torx socket [t1089]

## Parts

- [Partial] Exhaust nuts [t1089]
- FelPro header-to-head gaskets [t1089]
- Flat collector cat gasket [t1089]
- OEM exhaust studs: Short length preferred for headers [t1089]

## Tips & gotchas

- Stock manifolds use both long and short studs, but DT headers require only the short ones. [t1089]
- Watch out for stock studs breaking when trying to loosen old nuts. [t1089]
